exploration.title: Leaf Energy Lab
exploration.subject: Biology
exploration.summary: Test why extra light cannot replace water or carbon dioxide in photosynthesis.
exploration.question: Can extra light replace water as an input to photosynthesis?
exploration.explanation: Photosynthesis uses light energy to make sugars from water and carbon dioxide. The released oxygen comes from water. One required input cannot replace another, and real responses depend on more than this activity’s invented settings. Plants also respire day and night.

experiments.title: Test a missing resource
experiments.instruction: Predict whether changing light from 30 to 100 changes the activity index when water is 0 and carbon dioxide is held at 80. Run the fixed trials.
experiments.observe: Both trials show 0. Light supplies energy, but it cannot replace water as a matter input.

experiments.title: Find where light stops limiting
experiments.instruction: Hold water at 35 and carbon dioxide at 80. Predict the pattern for light settings 15, 35 and 100, then run all three trials.
experiments.observe: The index rises from 37 to 67, then stays at 67 because water limits the model above light 35.

exploration.misconception: Plants do not absorb sugar food from soil. Light supplies energy; water and carbon dioxide supply matter used to make sugars.
